authority: Advisory task-selection overlay only. WORK-QUEUE is priority authority; RELEASE-QUALITY-LEDGER alone owns passes.

entries.payoff: Avoid a second execution engine; reuse the already integrated pinned USA AOT guest while closing the actual Windows journey.
entries.trigger: Any change to the running game backend or native/Modern integration.
entries.action: Extend existing Baldosa guest/Modern C ABI and verified route instead of rebuilding a guest or introducing another game simulator.
entries.qualification: Authentic guest P1/P2 input, pause/result and lifecycle observed through the same host candidate, followed by the relevant independent QA.
entries.stop: Never declare a complete original event from short guest checks; retain legacy rollback.

entries.payoff: Reuse completed Modern frontend/controller state machines and avoid inventing another menu or session coordinator.
entries.trigger: Controller-first profile to race/result/Records workflow is incomplete.
entries.action: Bind the existing Modern states to Baldosa execution through the current typed host adapter and the original run/record stores.
entries.qualification: One authentic 1P plus local 2P journey, controller-only navigation, genuine results and restart-safe records on the same candidate.
entries.stop: Do not fabricate results, rewrite existing product ownership or substitute source-only component tests for a real journey.

entries.payoff: Let gameplay, renderer and Windows agents reuse one captured ROM/candidate/input provenance instead of recapturing the route.
entries.trigger: A real candidate route is captured for two or more existing test consumers.
entries.action: Extend existing evidence_contract.py and tool_interop.json to bind original/native observed P1/P2 input, SRAM and candidate hash to independently checked outputs.
entries.qualification: A single real route receipt with positive and missing/mismatched-input negative-path tests; existing QA judges each domain separately.
entries.stop: No second runner, release ledger or assumption that a stored script proves the guest consumed those masks.

entries.payoff: Turn route provenance into reusable evidence for several tests instead of repeated source/guest alignment investigations.
entries.trigger: A course route or original/native comparison must be replayed or published.
entries.action: Reuse Baldosa's route conventions, Malmazuke's replay manifest techniques and UR's existing controller_input adapters; record observed consumed masks, not just intended ones.
entries.qualification: One exact USA route with source-logged frame/controller consumption and a fail-closed mismatch case.
entries.stop: Do not change input frame offsets merely to make checksum agreement pass.

entries.payoff: Avoid parallel first-difference implementations and localize QA-01 disagreement using existing trace/checkpoint tools.
entries.trigger: A strict original/native event differs in timing or relevant state.
entries.action: Use the existing UR checkpoint/first-difference chain first, consulting Baldosa firstdiff and Malmazuke replay methods for bounded improvements.
entries.qualification: First relevant divergent writer or state boundary tied to exact source and guest clocks, with unmasked original endpoint.
entries.stop: Stale stack/cosmetic differences alone are not gameplay defects or acceptable result waivers.

entries.payoff: Reuse Malmazuke's complete 65816 indirect/stack/RMW decoder rather than individually reconstructing writer addresses for QA-01.
entries.trigger: Existing bounded trace cannot identify a NMI/stack or course-state writer and has pre-instruction registers/opcode bytes available.
entries.action: Pilot the cohesive MIT-licensed malmazuke access modes/derive plus coverage opcode dependencies read-only on one 3–5-frame original trace; keep UR trace acquisition.
entries.qualification: Run upstream ROM-free mode tests plus one real USA trace window, compare sampled effective addresses to existing reference watch results, reject missing register fields.
entries.stop: If source trace lacks register inputs, improve the existing capture schema first; never infer PAL/USA semantics from same address.

entries.payoff: Use Malmazuke's PPU/decode knowledge to select original-source discriminators instead of repeating graphics reconstruction.
entries.trigger: 2P racer occlusion or top-slot final-color ownership remains unresolved after current original source probes.
entries.action: Consult malmazuke PPU, Baldosa visible native renderer and UR original OAM/PPU probes; adapt only a read-only producer or decoder missing from UR.
entries.qualification: One original P1/P2 live source-visible test and native final pixel comparison that distinguishes sprite/BG/OBJ ordering.
entries.stop: Tile decoding, OAM rectangles or alpha-empty bottom slots do not establish the final visible pixel.

entries.payoff: Build on existing UR PPU direct-write/DMA lineage and reuse Malmazuke port chronology only for a concrete missing link.
entries.trigger: Live 2P source attribution needs a missing original DMA latch/register write or completion observation.
entries.action: Extend report_snes9x_dma_entry_provenance.py rather than adding another graphics tracer, using Malmazuke content/provenance as a selective algorithm reference.
entries.qualification: Exact original CPU write order, port latch/state and completed transfer contrasted with native output on bounded frames.
entries.stop: Descriptor creation or DMA-entry observation alone is not a completed VRAM/OAM/CGRAM transfer.

entries.payoff: Immediately query all imported Baldosa names and Malmazuke PAL annotations before hand-labeling an address.
entries.trigger: A source symbol, CPU address or game-state name is required for a current investigation.
entries.action: Run query_upstream_knowledge.py and existing Baldosa crosswalk first; link attributed external names in research notes, and promote only proven canonical concepts.
entries.qualification: Source commit and ROM region retained; USA original instruction/state check before any canonical docs/SYMBOLS.md promotion.
entries.stop: No global PAL shift, automatic name equivalence or new canonical symbol registry.

entries.payoff: Avoid redundant recompiler/emulator fixes when a pinned Baldosa framework delta solves a reproduced issue.
entries.trigger: A measured native M/X, clock, PPU or host-runtime failure persists in the exact Baldosa Windows candidate.
entries.action: Select a cohesive compatible Baldosa framework patch group using the existing delta inventory; keep an isolated rollback rather than rebasing everything.
entries.qualification: Failing reproducer before patch, targeted tests plus current 1P/2P source/state and packaging regression afterward; license reviewed.
entries.stop: Never bulk-merge dozens of independent patches or reinterpret existing accepted routes without cause.

entries.payoff: Avoid repeated expensive identical tests after a stable acceptance witness exists.
entries.trigger: A stable expensive CI gate has reproducible inputs and duplicated runs materially slow real work.
entries.action: Pilot Malmazuke's transitive Ninja dependency identity logic read-only against one existing UR gate; compare every relevant source, header, toolchain, fixture and candidate.
entries.qualification: Unchanged inputs permit citation in dry-run; actual transitive source/header/fixture/toolchain mutation forces rerun; missing inputs fail closed.
entries.stop: Do not enable a CI bypass or cache based only on filenames, SHA of one source or untested dependency closure.

entries.payoff: Spend recompilation optimization effort only on actual hot code instead of speculative low-level work.
entries.trigger: At least one complete USA original/native event is accepted and a repeatable Baldosa route is available.
entries.action: Use existing report_baldosa_tier2_route_coverage.py, then optionally port bounded Baldosa coverage/promote_roots techniques for the measured hot functions.
entries.qualification: Before/after route speed and strict accepted original/native gameplay/graphics regression on exact candidate.
entries.stop: No speculative framework or opcode promotion before valid real-route performance and parity baseline.

entries.payoff: Transfer Malmazuke's seeded differential fuzz discipline to widen course coverage only after the baseline oracle is dependable.
entries.trigger: A source-authentic complete USA event is independently accepted in the intended test family.
entries.action: Pilot 3–10 reproducible seeds through the existing original/native runner; use the malmazuke seed/shrink strategy, not its PAL native simulator as the oracle.
entries.qualification: Seeded replay can reproduce every novel counterexample, distinguishing false positives and source/guest clock models.
entries.stop: No broad fuzz campaign on an unaccepted comparison oracle.

entries.payoff: Expose shared source/tool opportunities in lane context without making every agent read three entire repositories.
entries.trigger: Every fresh agent selects a lane or starts a substantial task.
entries.action: Read one bounded lane context and reuse overlay; consult full upstream machinery only for relevant candidate paths, not all 35 rows.
entries.qualification: Unit test validates source-backed registry, lane filtering, sorting and nonpromotion; no duplicated live queue authority.
entries.stop: Do not replace WORK-QUEUE ownership or accumulate exhaustive intake notes in every prompt.
